overview: The HC-SR501 is entirely passive — unlike an ultrasonic or IR-reflectance sensor, it doesn't emit anything. Its white fresnel dome splits its field of view into multiple zones and focuses infrared radiation onto a pyroelectric element that reacts to a CHANGE in infrared levels, not to infrared itself; that's why it triggers on a person walking through the room but stays silent on a person sitting perfectly still (their body heat isn't changing). Two onboard trimpots (sensitivity and output-hold delay) and a trigger-mode jumper let it be tuned for different rooms without any code, which is exactly why it's the standard 'is anyone here' sensor for beginners despite being just three wires.
simpleSummary: A sensor that detects movement by noticing sudden changes in infrared heat, the same way many hallway lights turn on automatically.

specifications.detectionRange: Up to 7m, adjustable via sensitivity trimpot
specifications.outputSignal: TTL digital, 3.3V HIGH when motion detected
specifications.warmUpTime: ~60 seconds after power-on before readings stabilize
specifications.delayTimeAdjustable: ~3s - 300s output HIGH hold time, set via trimpot
specifications.triggerMode: Selectable via jumper: single-trigger (L) or repeatable-trigger (H)
specifications.lensType: Fresnel dome lens, passive infrared (no emitter)

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input to the onboard voltage regulator.
pinMap.gotcha: It happily runs from anywhere between 5V and 20V thanks to the onboard regulator, but the OUT pin only ever swings 0-3.3V regardless of input voltage — don't assume a 5V logic level here.

pinMap.name: OUT
pinMap.function: Digital output — goes HIGH when motion is detected within range and angle, staying HIGH for the delay time set by the onboard trimpot.
pinMap.gotcha: There's a roughly 60-second warm-up period after power-on where the sensor's internal IR baseline is still settling, causing false or erratic triggers — ignore readings during that first minute rather than assuming the sensor is broken.

useCases.title: Automatic light/appliance switch
useCases.scenario: Trigger a relay to turn on a light or fan when someone enters a room, and let the delay trimpot handle the auto-off timing.

useCases.title: Security alarm trigger
useCases.scenario: Sound a buzzer or send a notification the instant motion is detected in a monitored area.

useCases.title: Robot wake-from-sleep trigger
useCases.scenario: Keep a battery-powered robot in low-power sleep until a person walks nearby, saving power versus constantly polling a camera or ultrasonic sensor.

useCases.title: Motion-triggered camera recording
useCases.scenario: Only wake an ESP32-CAM or start recording when the PIR fires, saving storage and power versus continuous recording.

useCases.title: Pet feeder / interactive toy trigger
useCases.scenario: Detect an animal's movement nearby to trigger a feeding mechanism or a toy's response.

oftenConfusedWith: HC-SR04 (measures actual distance to a fixed target; a PIR only fires on a CHANGE in infrared signature, so it can't measure range and won't detect a person standing perfectly still)
Thermal Camera MLX90640 (a PIR gives one binary yes/no motion bit with no spatial detail; the thermal camera gives a full grid of actual temperature values)
oftenUpgradedTo: Thermal Camera MLX90640, for actual spatial and temperature detail instead of a single trigger bit
mmWave presence sensors, which detect stationary people and have no warm-up delay

beginnerMistakes: Testing immediately after power-up, before the ~60 second warm-up settles, and concluding the sensor is broken.
Not accounting for the ~120° wide detection cone — it fires on movement well off to the sides, not just dead ahead.
Mounting it behind glass or plastic — like most PIR sensors, it needs a direct IR path, and glass blocks or blurs it.
Forgetting the sensitivity and delay trimpots exist, and fighting long HIGH-hold times in software instead of just turning the delay pot down.
Assuming the OUT pin is 5V logic because VCC is fed 5V-20V, when OUT actually only ever outputs 3.3V.
